DNA (blue) nuclei are oval, smooth-bordered, uniform intensity in both treated and DMSO. No nuclear fragmentation, micronuclei, or chromatin condensation enrichment visible. data.note:
Correctly classified as Kinase inhibitors despite moderate confidence.

Unblinding confirms alsterpaullone (PubChem CID 5005498, structure match). ChEMBL has no curated MoA but BBBC021 annotates as Kinase inhibitor; literature identifies it as a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor inducing apoptosis via caspase-9/mitochondrial pathway (PMID 12669310) and general CDK inhibitor toxicity in HeLa (PMID 23577282), consistent with broader therapeutic CDK inhibition concept (PMID 10911915).

Phenotype observed: dose-dependent nuclear/cellular hypertrophy (nuc_major_axis rho +1.0, nuc_dna_mean rho -1.0, frac_large_nucleus z 25.5 at 30uM) with reduced DNA intensity (decondensed chromatin) and no tubulin/actin disruption or mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like non-significant, tub_mean rho 0). This matches CDK-mediated G1/G2 arrest and growth without division rather than Aurora/Eg5 (monopolar spindles, mitotic index increase), microtubule or actin disruptor signatures, or classic DNA damage/replication (gamma-H2AX foci, S-phase changes).

NSC vote 3/4 wells Kinase inhibitors (summed similarity 1.52, top neighbors PD-169316) supported by orthogonal dose responses and microscopy. Reflection: even with ChEMBL empty, phenotypic profile plus literature triangulates CDK inhibition; requested 0.023uM retest was infeasible due to budget but would have refined low-dose onset.

reflection.text:
Unblinded to alsterpaullone - truth Kinase inhibitors, agent Kinase inhibitors p=0.62 - verdict correct. Review requested repeat at 0.023 uM was not possible; budget was spent.

What got right:

 Acquisition covered the dynamic range: 0.1 uM (e2: nuc_major_axis z+4.4, nuc_solidity +3.2, 797 cells), 1 uM (e7: +5.9 / +4.5), 10 uM (e3: +9.1, nuc_dna_mean -5.1, eccentricity +3.3), 30 uM (e8: +17.7, frac_large_nucleus +25.5, nuc_dna_mean -12.4, 426 cells). Dose_response was monotonic and consistent: nuc_major_axis rho +1.00 p=0 (e12), nuc_dna_mean rho -1.00 p=0 (e10), nuc_dna_integrated rho -1.00 p=0 (e14), nuc_area rho +0.80 (e20) and cell_area rho +0.80 (e21). This hypertrophy with decondensed DNA plus reduced proliferation - cell_count rho -0.80 (e13) and microscopist density lower vs DMSO at 30uM (e17) - is the expected growth-arrest signature for a CDK inhibitor.

Comparison to reference atlas correctly anchored the call: NSC 2/2 (e4) then 3/4 Kinase inhibitors (e9). I kept Kinase 0.62 vs Aurora 0.12 / DNA damage 0.08 / DNA replication 0.05 (e18, e23) because the neighbor split was near-tie - Aurora 4/10, Kinase 3/10, DNA damage 3/10 at 4 wells (e9) - and required dose-dependent validation.

What ruled out alternatives was the lack of mitotic/microtubule signal: frac_mitotic_like rho -0.74 p=0.26 (e15), tub_mean rho 0.00 p=1 (e16), plus microscopist candidates unknown/none across low and high dose (e5, e6, e17). That allowed down-weighting Aurora/Eg5 and Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers despite large nuclei at 30uM which alone can mimic protein synthesis / polyploidy classes.

What misled or was weak:

 k-neighbour tie could have misled to Aurora - it rose to 4/10 at final vote (e9) while Kinase stayed 3/10. Large effect sizes alone (frac_large_nucleus z+25.5 e8) do not discriminate class without the dose slope and tub/mitotic negatives.
 Eccentricity flipped from -2.7 at 0.1uM (e2) to +3.3 at 10uM (e3) - inconsistent shape cue, not reliable. I used solidity instead which was consistently high then non-dose-dependent (e22 rho -0.60 p=0.4) to exclude actin.
 Formal significance weak for n=4 wells: frac_large_nucleus p=0.2 (e11), nuc_area p=0.2 (e20), cell_count p=0.2 (e13). I did not over-interpret p>0.05 but used direction plus independent rho -1.0/+1.0 hits.
 Acquisition choice used all 4 wells early (0.1,1,10,30uM) from 8 doses 0.01-30uM (e1). This captured the slope but left no well to test the requested 0.023 uM with larger IQR/adjacent strips; steps 23-24 correctly noted budget spent and re-analyzed adjacent covariates e20-e22 instead of new data.
 describe_phenotype was only 2 fields each (e5,e6,e17) - useful to exclude actin/tubulin but subjective threshold limited.

 Compound identity held: lookup showed name and BBBC021 structure agree for alsterpaullone PubChem 5005498 ChEMBL CHEMBL50894, mechanisms none curated (e25,e26), so atlas + phenotype carried the decision. Literature search PubMed 'alsterpaullone CDK kinase inhibitor mechanism' returned 3/3 (e27) - supports alsterpaullone as a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor PMID 12669310 and PMID 23577282, consistent with broad CDK inhibition concept PMID 10911915 - while 'CDK inhibitor cell hypertrophy senescence' returned 0 hits (e28), so that part of the phenotype interpretation remains claim without citation.
what_was_right: dose-dependent nuclear hypertrophy (nuc_major_axis e2,e7,e3,e8; e12 rho +1.0; e20,e21 rho +0.8; e8 frac_large_nucleus +25.5) with decondensed DNA (e10 rho -1.0, e14 rho -1.0, e3/e8 z -5.1/-12.4) and reduced count/density (e13,e17)
what_was_wrong: k-neighbour near-tie Aurora 4/10 vs Kinase 3/10 e9 could favor Aurora; eccentricity sign flip e2 vs e3 and non-significant p=0.2 for several dose_responses e11/e13/e20/e21 were weak; early spend of 4-well budget prevented testing requested 0.023uM e24

citations.claim: alsterpaullone described as novel cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor
Inhibition of CDKs as therapeutic modality - general CDK framework

reflection.next_experiment: If budget allowed: repeat 0.01-0.05uM range with larger IQR and adjacent-strip covariates to capture onset at 0.023uM, plus EdU/PI cell-cycle profiling and p-Rb western vs reference CDK inhibitor, and gamma-H2AX to exclude DNA damage; as proposed in conclusion evidence e9,e10,e12,e14-e17.

## Reflection

Unblinded to alsterpaullone - truth Kinase inhibitors, agent Kinase inhibitors p=0.62 - verdict correct. Review requested repeat at 0.023 uM was not possible; budget was spent.

What got right:

 Acquisition covered the dynamic range: 0.1 uM (e2: nuc_major_axis z+4.4, nuc_solidity +3.2, 797 cells), 1 uM (e7: +5.9 / +4.5), 10 uM (e3: +9.1, nuc_dna_mean -5.1, eccentricity +3.3), 30 uM (e8: +17.7, frac_large_nucleus +25.5, nuc_dna_mean -12.4, 426 cells). Dose_response was monotonic and consistent: nuc_major_axis rho +1.00 p=0 (e12), nuc_dna_mean rho -1.00 p=0 (e10), nuc_dna_integrated rho -1.00 p=0 (e14), nuc_area rho +0.80 (e20) and cell_area rho +0.80 (e21). This hypertrophy with decondensed DNA plus reduced proliferation - cell_count rho -0.80 (e13) and microscopist density lower vs DMSO at 30uM (e17) - is the expected growth-arrest signature for a CDK inhibitor.

Comparison to reference atlas correctly anchored the call: NSC 2/2 (e4) then 3/4 Kinase inhibitors (e9). I kept Kinase 0.62 vs Aurora 0.12 / DNA damage 0.08 / DNA replication 0.05 (e18, e23) because the neighbor split was near-tie - Aurora 4/10, Kinase 3/10, DNA damage 3/10 at 4 wells (e9) - and required dose-dependent validation.

What ruled out alternatives was the lack of mitotic/microtubule signal: frac_mitotic_like rho -0.74 p=0.26 (e15), tub_mean rho 0.00 p=1 (e16), plus microscopist candidates unknown/none across low and high dose (e5, e6, e17). That allowed down-weighting Aurora/Eg5 and Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers despite large nuclei at 30uM which alone can mimic protein synthesis / polyploidy classes.

What misled or was weak:

 k-neighbour tie could have misled to Aurora - it rose to 4/10 at final vote (e9) while Kinase stayed 3/10. Large effect sizes alone (frac_large_nucleus z+25.5 e8) do not discriminate class without the dose slope and tub/mitotic negatives.
 Eccentricity flipped from -2.7 at 0.1uM (e2) to +3.3 at 10uM (e3) - inconsistent shape cue, not reliable. I used solidity instead which was consistently high then non-dose-dependent (e22 rho -0.60 p=0.4) to exclude actin.
 Formal significance weak for n=4 wells: frac_large_nucleus p=0.2 (e11), nuc_area p=0.2 (e20), cell_count p=0.2 (e13). I did not over-interpret p>0.05 but used direction plus independent rho -1.0/+1.0 hits.
 Acquisition choice used all 4 wells early (0.1,1,10,30uM) from 8 doses 0.01-30uM (e1). This captured the slope but left no well to test the requested 0.023 uM with larger IQR/adjacent strips; steps 23-24 correctly noted budget spent and re-analyzed adjacent covariates e20-e22 instead of new data.
 describe_phenotype was only 2 fields each (e5,e6,e17) - useful to exclude actin/tubulin but subjective threshold limited.

 Compound identity held: lookup showed name and BBBC021 structure agree for alsterpaullone PubChem 5005498 ChEMBL CHEMBL50894, mechanisms none curated (e25,e26), so atlas + phenotype carried the decision. Literature search PubMed 'alsterpaullone CDK kinase inhibitor mechanism' returned 3/3 (e27) - supports alsterpaullone as a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor PMID 12669310 and PMID 23577282, consistent with broad CDK inhibition concept PMID 10911915 - while 'CDK inhibitor cell hypertrophy senescence' returned 0 hits (e28), so that part of the phenotype interpretation remains claim without citation.

What was right:
- dose-dependent nuclear hypertrophy (nuc_major_axis e2,e7,e3,e8; e12 rho +1.0; e20,e21 rho +0.8; e8 frac_large_nucleus +25.5) with decondensed DNA (e10 rho -1.0, e14 rho -1.0, e3/e8 z -5.1/-12.4) and reduced count/density (e13,e17)

What was wrong or missed:
- k-neighbour near-tie Aurora 4/10 vs Kinase 3/10 e9 could favor Aurora; eccentricity sign flip e2 vs e3 and non-significant p=0.2 for several dose_responses e11/e13/e20/e21 were weak; early spend of 4-well budget prevented testing requested 0.023uM e24
